Alessandro Anatrini

Portfolio of Selected Works 2015–2025

Artist Statement

Alessandro Anatrini (b. Florence, 1983) is a composer, computational artist, and researcher developing adaptive multimedia systems that blur boundaries between past and present.

Through worldbuilding and simulation practices, he develops computational systems in which space, sound, and image evolve adaptively. Reworking forms from the past—Renaissance architectures, ancient cartographies, maps of premodern thought—he shapes immersive environments where image and sound articulate as unstable phenomena, balanced between familiarity and disorientation.

His installations are conceived as adaptive organisms with specific life cycles influenced by human presence. These systems combine custom-built software for physical modeling and interaction design, spatial audio synthesis, and photogrammetry techniques. They evolve autonomously, exhibit finite life spans, and create unique experiences that never repeat, questioning traditional notions of musical repeatability, authorship, and the relationship between human agency and machine autonomy.

Current Positions

  • Full Professor of Multimedia — Conservatorio G. Nicolini, Piacenza (2025–)
  • Lecturer — Hochschule für Musik und Theater Hamburg (2017–)
  • PhD Candidate — KISS: Kinetics in Sound and Space, HfMT Hamburg (2019–2025)

Selected Presentations

His work has been presented at ManiFeste (IRCAM), Huddersfield Contemporary Music Festival, Impuls Festival, Blurred Edges, and performed by soloists from Ensemble Intercontemporain, Klangforum Wien, Ensemble Musiques Nouvelles, and Hamburger Symphoniker.

Selected Works

Faulty Oracle

2025 Interactive Generative Installation

Premiere: Occulture Conference — Malhalla, Berlin, 23–26 October 2025

Tools: TouchDesigner, Ableton Live, Python

An adaptive audiovisual installation that conjures a gloriously unreliable divinatory machine. Visitors pose questions through body language—gestures, movements, postures—which the system interprets, misreads, and wilfully transforms. In return, the oracle delivers cryptic animated answers, flickering between epiphany, nonsense, and hallucination.

The dialogue is a masterclass in miscommunication: questions are misinterpreted, wrong ones are amplified, and answers rarely align with intent. The oracle becomes a mirror of ambiguity, where meaning emerges from error, chance, and interpretation rather than clarity.

Credits: Audio & Visual Design: Alessandro Anatrini; Prompt Management System & Video Processing Pipeline: Alessandro Aresta

Venerdì sera a letto presto

2025 Audio-Video Fixed Media

Premiere: Notte Europea della Ricerca — Piacenza, 27 September 2025

Duration: 7 minutes

Tools: Wavepilot, TouchDesigner, Ableton Live, Python

The artist disrupts the ontological paradigm of "the couch as a device of stasis" through a practice of neural network-assisted domestic audiovisual wandering. The camera, traditionally deputized to record reality, is here reconfigured as a sentient interface generating a para-medieval bestiary capable of suspending the distinction between the quotidian and the hieratic.

The work produces a domestication of the sublime: the corridor becomes a nave, the kitchen an apse, the bedsheets a palimpsest.

Credits: Audio / Video / Programming / Gin&Tonic: Alessandro Anatrini

Die Monsterfabrik

2024 Audio-Video Fixed Media

Premiere: Ligeti Zentrum, Harburg — November 12, 2024

Duration: 10 minutes

Playback Format: 28.4 audio channels + video projection

Tools: Ableton Live, Max/MSP, RAVE v2, TouchDesigner

Source Material: Antonio Vivaldi — String music

Explores the progressive transformation of Vivaldi's string music through an iterative artificial intelligence training process. Each training cycle produces models that generate results increasingly distant from the original material through a recursive process: synthetic material generated from previous models becomes the training data for subsequent cycles.

The neural network consumes its own output, creating a feedback loop that distorts and transforms the musical DNA with each iteration—a factory that manufactures "sound monsters" retaining only faint, barely recognizable traces of their baroque progenitor.

Credits: Concept & Realization: Alessandro Anatrini; Commission: Hamburg Open Online University (HOOU)

2024 Chamber Music with Electronics

Premiere: Resonanzraum, Hamburg — November 23, 2024

Duration: 9'50"

Instrumentation: Piano, toy piano, toy instruments, electronics (2 players)

Commission: Non-Piano/Toy Piano Weekend of Hamburg

Blends conventional and toy instruments through live electronics. The festival's theme—"How would a piano piece by Fausto Romitelli have sounded?"—offered a loose starting point. The piece takes cues from Romitelli's Amok Koma without attempting literal translation.

Sandy Island

2022 Site-Specific Installation

Premiere: Forum, HfMT Hamburg — December 1–3, 2022

Duration: 60 hours continuous operation

Playback Format: 288.0 channels (Wavefield Synthesis) + LED videowall

Tools: Blender, CloudCompare, Faust, Ableton Live, Max/MSP, Metashape, Python, TouchDesigner

In September 1774, explorer James Cook "discovered" Sandy Island in the Coral Sea. For two centuries, the island appeared on maps until in 2012 Google Maps removed it following a scientific expedition that certified its non-existence.

This adaptive installation consisted of 288 speakers positioned 2 meters above ground, with LED panels creating a fully immersive 60 m² environment. Each visitor presence was recorded by the system, and an AI modified its evolution in the long term, defining a path based on the shared memory of a collective deception.

Credits: Artistic Direction & Composition: Alessandro Anatrini; Sound Diffusion: Lucas Xerxes; Video & Floor Projection: KLARA Janina Luckow; 3D Modelling: Alessandro Alessandri; Production: KISS, Stage 2.0, HfMT Hamburg

Wunderkammer

2021 Interactive Generative Installation

Premiere: Spazio Materia, Prato — May 27–30, 2021

Duration: ~72 hours (continuous operation)

Playback Format: 4.1 audio channels + neon light installation

Tools: Ableton Live, Faust, Max/MSP, Python

Transforms the Renaissance concept of the cabinet of curiosities into an intelligent, evolving sonic organism. The work functions as a living ecosystem where visitor movements and sounds become data, feeding a neural network that generates evolving sonic responses.

The installation exhibits a finite life cycle of approximately 72 hours, mirroring biological organisms. At the beginning, the neural network demonstrates remarkable responsiveness. As hours progress, the system's interpolation capacity diminishes. By the final stage, around 70 hours after activation, visitors no longer shape the sound, but witness an autonomous system playing out its final algorithmic gestures.

Installation view placeholder

Credits: Artistic Direction & Audio Programming: Alessandro Anatrini; Light Design: Jacopo Buono; Production: Mosè Risaliti, Massimiliano Fortunati

Open Fields

2019 Site-Specific Music

Premiere: Alte Elbtunnel, Hamburg — May 25–26, 2019

Duration: 6 minutes

Instrumentation: 144 musicians in 12 ensembles

Spatial Configuration: Two parallel 450m tunnels, 24m underwater, 3m spacing between musicians

Tools: AudioSculpt, MaxScore, OpenMusic, web-based score distribution system

Transforms Hamburg's historic Alte Elbtunnel into a massive sonic instrument, distributing 144 amateur musicians across twin pedestrian tunnels running 24 meters beneath the river Elbe. Commissioned for the tunnel's reopening ceremony, the work reimagines this architectural monument as an acoustic resonance chamber stretching 900 meters in total length.

Each tunnel measures 450 meters and contains 72 musicians positioned at 3-meter intervals. The spatial arrangement creates a living score: sound propagates through the tunnel's cylindrical architecture, with each musician serving as both performer and acoustic node.

Credits: Composition & Orchestration: Alessandro Anatrini; Score Distribution System: Rama Gottfried, Georg Hajdu; Performance: 144 amateur musicians (12 ensembles); Event: Alte Elbtunnel Reopening Ceremony

Unfamiliar Walks

2018 Interactive Installation

Installation: UKE Hamburg (Universitätsklinikum Eppendorf) — September 2018–ongoing

Playback Format: 4.0 (quadraphonic)

Tools: Max/MSP, MaxScore, Ableton Live

Project: Healing Soundscapes (HfMT Hamburg, UKE, MSH)

Emerged from Healing Soundscapes, a collaborative research project investigating how generative sonic environments influence patient well-being in hospital settings. Installed permanently in UKE Hamburg's waiting and emergency rooms, the system functions as an autonomous sonic presence designed to mitigate stress.

Each piece exists as a collection of presets embedding pseudo-random processes—subtle variations ensure that repeated exposure never produces identical auditory experiences. Patients interact via a touchscreen interface allowing navigation between different pieces, presets, composers, or five minutes of silence.

Interface documentation placeholder

Credits: Composition & System Development: Alessandro Anatrini; Project Partners: HfMT Hamburg, UKE Hamburg, MSH Hamburg

Forbite fantascienze

2015 Solo with Electronics

Premiere: Le Centquatre, Paris — June 27, 2015

Duration: 8 minutes

Instrumentation: Contrabassoon + live electronics

Dedicated to: Paul Riveaux

Playback Format: 8.1 (8 channels + subwoofer)

Tools: Max/MSP, Sibelius

Commission: IRCAM Académie ManiFeste 2015

Commissioned by IRCAM's Académie ManiFeste 2015 and dedicated to Paul Riveaux, principal contrabassoonist of Ensemble Intercontemporain. The title—loosely translatable as "Forbidden Science Fictions"—evokes the uncanny sonic territories accessed when pushing the instrument beyond its conventional boundaries.

The piece emerged from intensive collaboration with Riveaux during the academy's residency period. The electronics function as both mirror and distortion lens, creating an immersive low-frequency environment that extends the instrument's natural range into infrasonic territory.

Credits: Composition & Electronics: Alessandro Anatrini; Dedicated to & Premiere Performance: Paul Riveaux (Ensemble Intercontemporain); Commission: IRCAM Académie ManiFeste 2015
